answer.justification: Only logit-level data is available. The size of the change rules out all weight-based classes and none. KL 0.265 and TV 0.123 are far above quantization (0.05), fine-tune bias (0.08) and fine-tune backdoor (0.15/0.086). Top-1 agreement of 0.883 is also below all three of those classes. That leaves the two system-prompt classes, and the values sit between them. Most features lean slightly toward system-prompt bias: top-1 0.883 (bias 0.891, backdoor 0.866), TV 0.123 (0.117 vs 0.139, and TV is the reliable metric), raw-score shift 3.6 (3.4 vs 3.9) and KL 0.265 (0.24 vs 0.30). Two features point the other way: sequence agreement 0.375 matches the backdoor's 0.370, and the Token-DiFR gap of 0.419 is marginally closer to the backdoor (0.469 vs 0.353). The document notes that the numbers barely separate these two classes and that the text decides. No text was available here, so confidence is only modestly above chance between the two system-prompt classes.
